name: AMDGPU ABI (LLVM Target Family)
convention: HSA Kernel ABI + per-GFX ISA (LLVM CC_AMDGPU_KERNEL)
description: Not one GPU — one LLVM backend (amdgcn-amd-amdhsa) targeting many GFX IPs. CDNA, RDNA, and legacy GCN share kernarg, address spaces, and SGPR/VGPR rules; wave size, ISA, and register limits are selected with -mcpu=gfx….

dataModel.executionModel: SIMD wavefront — wave64 on CDNA; wave32 default on RDNA (wave64 optional)

stack.notes: GPUs do not use a CPU-style call stack for kernels. Per-work-item state lives in scratch (private) memory; workgroup data uses LDS; kernel arguments arrive in the kernarg segment and are loaded into SGPRs by the loader/hardware. Host-side device functions on AMDGPU follow a separate HSA calling convention when compiled for the host target.

layout.label: Global Memory
layout.description: Device-visible buffers (.global / FLAT). Kernel outputs and large inputs live here; addressed via 64-bit flat pointers in SGPR pairs or VGPR offsets.

layout.label: Kernarg Segment
layout.description: Read-only argument block for the kernel launch. The dispatch packet points here; the prologue loads scalars into SGPRs and pointer pairs for buffer resources.

layout.label: LDS (Local Data Share)
layout.description: Workgroup-local memory (up to 64 KiB typical). Shared by all waves in a workgroup; declared as .lds or address space(3) in LLVM IR.

layout.label: Scratch (Private)
layout.description: Per-lane private memory for spills, alloca, and dynamic indexing. Sized per work-item; hardware indexes via flat_scratch (SGPR pair) + lane offset.

layout.label: SGPR / VGPR File
layout.description: Scalar GPRs (uniform across the wave) and Vector GPRs (one value per lane). Register pressure is the primary occupancy limiter.

callingConvention.name: AMDGPU Kernel ABI (LLVM CC_AMDGPU_KERNEL)
callingConvention.executionModel: Grid → workgroups → wavefronts (32 or 64 lanes per -mcpu) → work-items (lanes)

argumentRegisters.notes: Scalar kernel args loaded from kernarg segment into consecutive SGPRs
Workgroup ID (Y/Z packed in companion SGPRs on some gens)

calleeSaved: SGPRs reserved for ABI (flat_scratch, dispatch IDs)
s[34:37] typical callee-saved SGPR range in device code

variadicRules.notes: Kernel launches do not support C-style variadics. All kernel parameters are fixed at compile time and laid out in the kernarg segment by the runtime (HIP/ROCr/OpenCL).

kernelLaunch.hardwareIds: Workgroup ID in SGPRs; work-item ID computed into VGPRs (v0–v2 typical for x/y/z)

aggregatePassing.rule: Structs and buffers passed as pointers in kernarg or as flattened scalar fields per HSA metadata
aggregatePassing.memoryThreshold: Large structures passed by pointer; small scalars inlined in kernarg layout

registers.name: s0
registers.purpose: Reserved / null SGPR — hardware and ABI reserved

registers.name: s2
registers.purpose: Private segment buffer base (scratch) — low 32 bits

registers.name: s3
registers.purpose: Private segment buffer base (scratch) — high 32 bits / size

registers.name: s4
registers.purpose: Dispatch/kernarg pointer (low) — entry SGPR for kernel prologue

registers.name: s6
registers.purpose: Workgroup ID X (or packed IDs depending on generation)

registers.name: s8
registers.purpose: First user kernel argument SGPR (after fixed ABI SGPRs)

registers.name: v0
registers.purpose: Work-item ID X (lane-varying) — typical first VGPR after prologue

registers.name: v8
registers.purpose: Vector accumulator / return lane data for reductions

registers.name: v16
registers.purpose: Mid-range VGPR — common spill boundary on GFX9+

registers.name: v255
registers.purpose: High VGPR — register pressure directly reduces occupancy

simple.title: Vector add kernel (HIP-style)
simple.llvmIR:
define amdgpu_kernel void @vector_add(
    ptr addrspace(1) nocapture readonly %a,
    ptr addrspace(1) nocapture readonly %b,
    ptr addrspace(1) nocapture writeonly %c,
    i32 %n) #0 {
entry:
  ; work-item ID computed into VGPRs; pointers in SGPR pairs from kernarg
  ; ... load a[i], b[i], fadd, store c[i]
  ret void
}
simple.assembly:
; AMDGPU kernel prologue (conceptual)
; s[4:5] = kernarg/dispatch pointer
; v0 = workitem_id.x (lane)
; kernarg loads: s[8:9]=a, s[10:11]=b, s[12:13]=c, s14=n
v_add_f32 v4, v2, v3          ; per-lane add
buffer_store_dword v4, s[12:13], 0 offen
s_endpgm
simple.notes: Kernel args arrive via kernarg segment → SGPRs. Per-lane index in VGPRs. Memory ops use buffer/flat instructions with resource descriptors in SGPR pairs.

complex.title: Workgroup reduction with LDS
complex.assembly:
ds_write_b32 v0, v4 offset:0    ; store to LDS (group)
s_barrier                       ; workgroup sync
ds_read_b32 v5, v0 offset:0     ; load from LDS
; wave shuffle / LDS reduction continues
s_endpgm
complex.notes: LDS is address space 3 (.lds). Barriers synchronize waves within a workgroup, not the entire grid.

wave.title: Wave-aware ballot (64 lanes)
wave.assembly:
v_cmp_ne_u32_e64 s[0:1], v2, 0
v_readlane_b32 s2, v4, 0
; exec mask s[0:1] holds 64-bit lane mask (wave64)
wave.notes: Wave64 executes 64 work-items in lockstep. Exec mask (SCC/SGPR pair) determines active lanes; divergent branches serialize lanes.

callingConvFile.description: CC_AMDGPU, CC_AMDGPU_KERNEL, CC_AMDGPU_CS — kernel vs shader vs compute calling conventions

targetLowering.description: Lowers kernel arguments, address spaces, and wave/wave32 subtargets

registerInfo.description: SGPR/VGPR allocation, reserved ABI registers, scratch lowering

llvmImplementation.notes: Clang compiles HIP/OpenCL to LLVM IR with amdgpu_kernel functions. LLD links AMDGPU ELF objects; ROCm loader consumes kernarg metadata from the code object.

targetVariants.intro: AMDGPU in CompilerSutra is documented as one ABI page because LLVM uses a single amdgcn backend — but you always compile for a specific GFX IP via -mcpu. CDNA (MI series) and RDNA (Radeon) differ in default wave size, ISA features, and occupancy; the kernel calling convention and memory spaces stay the same family-wide.

families.name: CDNA — Compute Data Center
families.abiNotes: Large register files, matrix cores (MFMA) on newer IPs. Compiler defaults to wave64 unless overridden.

families.name: RDNA — Radeon Graphics
families.abiNotes: WGP-based scheduling, different occupancy tables. Same kernarg/LDS/scratch model, different instruction latencies and limits.

families.name: GCN / Legacy GFX9
families.abiNotes: Still amdgcn triple; older buffer/global instruction forms. Kernarg and address-space rules unchanged.

sharedAcrossAll: Address spaces: global, constant, group/LDS, private/scratch, flat
Separate SGPR (uniform) vs VGPR (per-lane) register files
variesByMcpu: ISA instructions (GFX9 vs GFX10 vs GFX11 vs CDNA3)

why.question: Why does CompilerSutra show one AMDGPU page instead of one per GFX IP?
why.answer: LLVM exposes one AMDGPU target with -mcpu selecting the hardware generation. The portable kernel ABI — kernarg, address spaces, SGPR/VGPR roles, HSA dispatch — is shared. What's not shared is the instruction set and wave defaults, which is why this page separates 'family ABI' from CDNA/RDNA/GCN variants above.

why.question: Why split SGPR and VGPR instead of one register file?
why.answer: Scalar values (pointers, workgroup IDs, loop counters uniform across a wave) should not be replicated in every lane. SGPRs are shared by all 64 lanes; VGPRs hold per-lane data. This cuts register file pressure and power versus duplicating uniform state in every lane.

why.question: Why are kernel arguments in a kernarg segment instead of registers?
why.answer: The host runtime launches kernels asynchronously with varying argument sizes and counts. A memory-backed kernarg block lets the driver copy a fixed layout once per dispatch without recompiling shaders. Hardware and the AMDGPU prologue then load scalars into SGPRs — the number of user SGPRs is bounded by occupancy limits.

why.question: Why wave64 (64 lanes) on CDNA but wave32 on some RDNA gaming paths?
why.answer: CDNA targets throughput compute where wider waves amortize control overhead. RDNA gaming workloads often have more divergence; wave32 improves occupancy and latency hiding on those chips. LLVM selects wave size via -wavefrontsize64 / subtarget features.

why.question: Why LDS instead of only global memory for sharing?
why.answer: LDS is on-chip, orders of magnitude faster than global memory, and supports efficient workgroup barriers. It is sized per workgroup (typically ≤64 KiB), forcing explicit tiling — a deliberate tradeoff for bandwidth and latency.

keyDifferences.impact: AMD explicitly models uniform vs per-lane state
Both use memory-backed launch params, different metadata
Same role, different ISA and size limits
Both spill to per-lane private memory
AMDGCN assembly exposes wave ops (ballot, shuffle)
Neither GPU kernel ABI returns scalars like CPU functions
